title: Acute inflammation
subtitle: Understand the response. Connect the mediators. Remember the sequence.
author: Medical lecture collection

blocks.text: Acute inflammation is a rapid protective response that delivers leukocytes and plasma proteins to sites of infection or tissue injury.

blocks.title: Clinical anchor
blocks.text: Warmth, erythema, swelling, pain, and loss of function arise from vasodilation, permeability, and mediator activity.
Explore the response one step at a time. Select a stage to focus on its place in the sequence.

blocks.title: From tissue injury to exudate
blocks.description: Follow the sequence from top to bottom. Expand a step when more detail is available.

steps.title: Tissue injury
steps.description: Begin with the site of infection or tissue injury.

steps.title: Mediator release
steps.description: Connect histamine and nitric oxide with the vascular response.

steps.title: Vasodilation
steps.description: Relate increased blood flow to warmth and erythema.

steps.title: Permeability
steps.description: Consider how vascular permeability contributes to swelling.

steps.title: Exudate
steps.description: Remember the defining feature: a protein-rich fluid.

blocks.label: Exam pearl
blocks.text: Exudate has high protein content; transudate is protein-poor and usually caused by altered hydrostatic or oncotic pressure.

blocks.prompt: Which mediator is a potent chemotactic factor for neutrophils?
blocks.answer: C5a. It is a complement split product that recruits and activates leukocytes.
Exudate is protein-rich. Transudate is protein-poor and usually reflects altered hydrostatic or oncotic pressure.

blocks.title: Before you move on
items: I can name the cardinal signs
I can distinguish exudate from transudate
I can trace the vascular response
I can match each mediator to its effects
